    President Trump fired Attorney General
    Pam Bondi on April 2, 2026, after a turbulent 14-month tenure, driven by frustration over her handling of the Jeffrey Epstein files and failure to aggressively prosecute political opponents. Trump, who described the move as a transition, was dissatisfied with her execution of his agenda. 
    Key Reasons for Bondi's Firing: 
    • Epstein Files Handling: Bondi faced intense criticism for her management of the release of Jeffrey Epstein files, which were heavily redacted. Trump and his supporters were disappointed that the release did not lead to major prosecutions and that she appeared to contradict other administration officials.
    • Failed Prosecutions: Trump felt that Bondi failed to sufficiently investigate and prosecute his political enemies, despite efforts to align the Department of Justice (DOJ) with his personal agenda.
    • Rising Frustration: A "heated confrontation" at the White House last week further contributed to the decision.
    • Ongoing Investigations: She was facing a scheduled deposition by the House Oversight Committee regarding the Epstein investigation.
    • Political Missteps: While trying to satisfy Trump's demands, she failed to garner trust, as Trump felt she did not fully act on his vision. 
    Bondi was replaced by her deputy, Todd Blanche, on an interim basis.
